tagline: A four-lane toll road shares its corridor with a paved recreation trail.
intro: The Suncoast Scenic Parkway carries four lanes of limited-access traffic through Hillsborough, Pasco and Hernando counties, alongside a trail for non-motorized travel. Florida Scenic Highways describes the 42-mile corridor as a design intended to fit its natural surroundings while serving transportation and outdoor fitness. It received scenic-highway designation on August 18, 2006. For most of the way, fences and grass separate the trail from the traffic; in places, concrete barriers divide them. The trail connects with other multi-use paths, recreation areas and nature parks.

Construction began in 1998, and the parkway opened in two stages in 2001. The first reached State Road 50 in February; the northern section continued to US 98 that August. A paved recreation trail opened with the highway, running along its western side. River and stream bridges were made wide enough to carry trail users too. At designation, it was Florida’s only controlled-access road recognized as an official Florida Scenic Highway.

Southbound, the scenic drive begins at US 98 and ends at Van Dyke Road in Hillsborough County. The trail crosses State Road 50 on its own overpass near Brooksville. Farther south, four miles north of State Road 54, a separate paved trail connects to J. B. Starkey Wilderness Park.

moments.title: Suncoast Trail
moments.text: Near Brooksville, the Suncoast Trail crosses State Road 50 on a dedicated overpass west of the parkway. Elsewhere, the two routes share river and stream bridges built wide enough for trail users. For most of its length, the trail keeps close to the highway, separated by fences, grass and sometimes concrete barriers. Where roads pass above the parkway, especially north of State Road 52, the trail briefly leaves its side to cross those roads at ground level. Signs regulate minor crossings, while pedestrian signals serve busier intersections. Motor vehicles are prohibited on the trail except for rangers and other authorized users.

moments.title: Starkey Wilderness Park connector
moments.text: Four miles north of State Road 54, a 6.5-mile paved bicycle trail links the Suncoast Trail with J. B. Starkey Wilderness Park in New Port Richey. The connection is part of a larger corridor whose trail links recreation areas, nature parks and other multi-use trails.

moments.title: Odessa
moments.text: Odessa’s transport story reaches back to the Orange Belt Railway. Peter Demens, a Russian immigrant who developed the community through the railway, named it in the 1880s. He also founded St. Petersburg, giving both communities names of places he had visited in Russia. The railroad ran parallel to State Road 54. A large local sawmill replaced smaller mills before burning in 1922. The area’s open spaces, ranches and horse properties have since given way to many suburban developments as Tampa expands. Tampa Bay Executive Airport was another transport presence here until 2004.

practical: Suncoast Trail: The Suncoast Parkway is a toll road operated by Florida’s Turnpike Enterprise. (checked 2026-10-11)
